rot.ideia.ex1.e1: Now the rook has a helper: the bishop. The rook cuts ranks and files; the bishop, diagonals.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: The bishop works from afar. From b1 here, it attacks h7, on the other side of the board.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: Your king guards g7. With h7 attacked by the bishop, only the rook's check on the edge is missing.
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: Checkmate! The rook attacks the edge, the bishop guards h7 and the king guards g7.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The rook goes to a8 and checks along the edge. Every escape square is taken.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.b1a2.1: The bishop left the h7 diagonal, and there was no check.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.b1a2.2: The black king runs to h7.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.b1a2.3: Let's go back: the bishop stays, and the rook checks on the edge.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not give mate. Let's go back to the position.
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: Remember: the bishop takes the escape square from afar, and the rook closes the edge.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: Here, if the rook checks on the edge now, the black king escapes through h7.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: First take the bishop to the diagonal that goes through h7. Then comes the mate.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: Prepare the mate with the bishop, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! From d3, the bishop attacks h7. The black king only has g8.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The bishop goes to d3 and attacks h7. The black king is left with only g8.
rot.ideia.ex2.alt.f1c4.1: That works too! The bishop takes g8, the king goes to h7, and the rook mates along the h-file.
rot.ideia.ex2.alt.f1c4.2: Look also at d3: the bishop takes h7, and the rook mates along the edge.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.a1a8.1: It is check, but h7 is still free.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.a1a8.2: The black king escapes to h7.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.a1a8.3: Let's go back: first the bishop, then the rook.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not prepare the mate. Let's go back to the position.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: Prepare the mate with the bishop, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: The black king goes to g8, its only square.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: Checkmate! The bishop guards h7, the king guards f7 and g7.
rot.ideia.ex2.l3: Now I will show the net of rook, bishop and king, and a danger: stalemate.
rot.demos.rede.e1: The black king is on the edge. Watch rook, bishop and king take all its squares together.
rot.demos.rede.l1: The bishop goes to g5 and takes h6.
rot.demos.rede.l2: The black king goes to h7.
rot.demos.rede.l3: The white king comes close and takes g8 and g6.
rot.demos.rede.l4: The black king only has h8.
rot.demos.rede.l5: Checkmate along the h-file! Each piece guards a part.
rot.demos.afogamento.e1: Now a danger. Count the black king's squares: your king guards g7 and h7. Only g8 is left.
rot.demos.afogamento.l1: If the bishop went to c4, it would take g8 without check. The black king would have no move: stalemate, a draw.
rot.demos.afogamento.l2: So do not move the bishop: give the rook check right away. Checkmate!
rot.demos.afogamento.l3: Now it's your turn: cut with the rook, take squares with the bishop and count squares before the mate.
rot.pratica.preparar.enunciado: Give checkmate. The black king has a7 and b8. First the bishop takes a7, then the rook closes the edge.
rot.pratica.preparar.fim: Perfect. The bishop took a7, and the rook gave mate.
rot.pratica.preparar.err.h1h8: It is check, but the king escapes through a7. Try again.
rot.pratica.centro.enunciado: Start in the center: cut the king with the rook, bring your king close and use the bishop to take squares.
rot.pratica.centro.fim: Well done. You knew how to use the bishop.
